newsitem.title: USA: Gaylord sees strong linerboard demand.
newsitem.headline: Gaylord sees strong linerboard demand.

text.p: Gaylord Container Corp said on Tuesday demand for linerboard was significant right now and it expected linerboard price increases in 1997 and 1998.

"It (1996) has been a roller-coaster year but demand is significant right now, so as you look into the future -- 1997 and perhaps 1998 -- what you see is a very encouraging scenario around demand, and we have plenty of capacity to deal with it as an industry," said Marvin Pomerantz, Gaylord Container chairman and chief executive officer.
Pomerantz said Gaylord believed the world economy would post good growth over the next few years.
Increased demand was also a function of balancing supply and demand and inventory, he said.
"In the quarter ending September we're now ahead in the United States in box shipments over a year ago," Pomerantz told Reuters in an interview.

He said he expected a $30 to $50 per ton linerboard price increase in 1997 and another one or two price increases in 1998. Linerboard prices increased $30 a ton in the United States in October, he said.

Linerboard price increases were generating increases in box prices, Pomerantz said, adding U.S. box prices had been a question in the industry. "We expect to see significant passthrough in terms of higher linerboard prices translating into higher box prices," he said.
Overcapacity has been an issue in the industry in 1996 and should extend into 1997 and perhaps into 1998, Pomerantz said. But production was no greater than it was at the end of 1995, Pomerantz said.
Gaylord's inventory were well balanced at the moment, he said but the company would not hesitate to take more downtime at certain mills if it needed to balance its inventory.
Gaylord is based in Deerfield, Ill.
